issues.issue: The 1.0 content lock describes a game nobody is scheduled to build. Phase 6 freezes scope at '3 arena biomes, 3 weapons/stances, 6 enemy types, 3 bosses', but no phase contains the work: Phase 3 builds boss #1, Phase 4 builds drafts/mutators/meta, Phase 5 is pure distribution, and Phase 6 (weeks 24-36) is Next Fest, accessibility, localization, AND launch. Biomes 2-3, weapons 2-3, enemies 4-6, and bosses 2-3 — easily 8-12 part-time weeks of content plus balance — appear only inside the lock document. This is the hidden 30% that turns a 9-month plan into 13 months.
issues.fix: Either schedule the content explicitly (insert a dedicated content phase between current Phases 4 and 5, accepting a later launch) or shrink the lock to what the plan actually produces: 1-2 biomes (palette/prop swaps of the existing arena are cheap), 2 weapons, 4-5 enemies via the affix multiplier already planned, 2 bosses. The mutator/affix system in Phase 4 is the honest content engine — lean on it and stop promising hand-built variety the calendar can't fund.

issues.issue: The three.js r128 -> r155+ upgrade is unnecessary risk with zero player-facing payoff, and it contradicts the roadmap's own principles ('the feel is the product', 'no TypeScript rewrite for its own sake'). The jump is ~30 majors of breaking changes: color management (sRGB output default), physically-correct lights with the new intensity model, renderer API churn — every hand-tuned light, fog, and material in a game whose entire pitch is 'hand-tuned feel' gets relit. '2 weeks timeboxed' part-time is ~20-25 hours; relighting alone can eat that. r128 vendored locally (Phase 0 already does this) is a perfectly safe runtime for a 1430-line game with no dependencies. The fallback clause ('ship on r128 and finish after') reveals the team already knows the upgrade isn't needed.
issues.fix: Cut the engine upgrade from the pre-1.0 plan entirely; move it to the post-launch icebox. Keep the valuable half of Tech Week — Vite + ES-module split along existing section comments and the damageEnemy/damageAlly unification — which is ~3-4 days, low-risk, and actually enables the Phase 4 feature growth. That frees ~1.5 weeks for the content gap in issue #1.

issues.issue: The free-forever web build and the $4.99 Steam build are never differentiated. Phase 0 declares 'this web build stays alive forever as the funnel', CrazyGames gets the full game with ads, the Steam demo is 'first 10 waves + boss' — so at launch the paid product's only stated delta over three free versions is achievements and cloud save. This is the classic web-to-Steam cannibalization trap; reviews will say 'this is free in your browser'. Relatedly, the wishlist math (2k by Next Fest, ~5k at launch) assumes browser-portal players convert to Steam wishlists, which historically they do at very poor rates — portal audiences and Steam buyers barely overlap.
issues.fix: Write the paid-delta decision into Phase 5 before the Steam page goes up. Viable split: web/portal builds get waves 1-10 + daily seed (the funnel and viral loop); Steam 1.0 exclusively gets endless mode, all bosses past the first, the full unlock board, leaderboards, and offline play. Treat web-derived wishlists as a bonus, not the plan: budget the GIF/social cadence and the Next Fest demo as the primary wishlist drivers, and set the launch go/no-go on wishlists from those channels.

issues.issue: One-shot launch channels are fired at the wrong build. Phase 3 spends Show HN and r/WebGames on the public beta — before the draft system, run arc, victory condition, daily seed, and meta progression (all Phase 4) exist. Show HN works once per project; r/WebGames effectively once. The roadmap burns its two biggest free traffic spikes on the version of the game its own thesis says lacks 'memory, variance, arc, and stakes', then has nothing equivalent left for when the addiction loop is actually proven.
issues.fix: Phase 3 goes soft-public only: itch page live, r/playmygame, Discord playtest servers — channels that tolerate iteration. Hold Show HN, r/WebGames, and the 'procedural rigs in one JS file' devlog for the Phase 4 exit, when retry rate >65% is demonstrated and the daily-seed share string gives spike traffic somewhere to stick. The devlog angle is genuinely HN-bait; don't waste it on a beta.

issues.issue: Savegame integrity on the actual deployment targets is unexamined, and it undermines the plan's self-declared strongest retention mechanic. The 'best score survives a reload' exit criterion will be tested on localhost but the game ships inside itch.io and CrazyGames iframes, where localStorage is third-party storage: Safari ITP partitions or evicts it, Firefox ETP partitions it, private windows drop it, and browsers evict it under storage pressure. Players' best scores and (later) the entire Valor/unlock board can silently vanish — on exactly the platforms where validation happens. There is also no migration story when a player moves from itch to CrazyGames to Steam (different origins = progress lost at each graduation).
issues.fix: Make the Phase 1 persistence module a storage facade from day one: localStorage fallback behind an interface, CrazyGames SDK data module backend in Phase 5 (it exists precisely because of this problem), Steamworks cloud backend for Tauri. Add a cheap export/import save code (base64 of the versioned schema) on the settings screen — it doubles as cross-platform migration. Amend the Phase 1 exit criterion to 'best score survives a reload inside the itch.io embed in Safari'.

issues.issue: Phase 5 is the most overloaded phase in the plan and contains its biggest unprototyped technical bet. In 6 part-time weeks: Steam page + capsule + trailer, CrazyGames SDK integration, Tauri wrapper, Steamworks integration, controller support, full key rebinding, settings completion, demo build, Armor Games outreach. The Tauri bet specifically: Steamworks from Tauri needs native Rust bindings, and the Steam overlay is notoriously broken over OS webviews (WKWebView/WebView2) — overlay, screenshots (F12), and Steam Input often fail, which players and reviews notice. Discovering this in week 20 of a 36-week plan blows the Next Fest deadline.
issues.fix: Spike the desktop wrapper in Phase 3's tech window instead: 2-3 days to stand up Tauri+steamworks-rs AND an Electron+steamworks.js equivalent, verify overlay, achievements, and controller input on Windows specifically (the market). Pick whichever works; Electron's larger binary is irrelevant for a $4.99 action game and it is the proven path (Vampire Survivors shipped on it). Then split Phase 5: CrazyGames first (pure web, fastest revenue), Steam infrastructure second.

issues.issue: The calendar counts in week numbers but Steam Next Fest runs on fixed dates (roughly February, June, October) with registration deadlines weeks earlier, and store pages need Valve review (2-5 business days) plus a 2-week minimum public-page age before a fest. 'Phase 6, weeks 24-36' either happens to straddle a fest or it doesn't — and a miss means a ~4-month slip or entering underprepared, which the roadmap's own 2k-wishlist gate forbids. Same blind spot for the 'page public in week 1 of Phase 5' item: capsule art and a trailer that pass Valve review are scheduled with zero days of buffer.
issues.fix: Anchor the plan to real dates now: pick the target fest (from a June 2026 start, the February 2027 fest is the realistic one), back-schedule registration, demo-build review, and the 2k-wishlist checkpoint from it, and add a written decision date ('if <2k wishlists by [date], we skip to June 2027 and Phase 6 becomes content polish'). Float the phase boundaries; never float the fest.

issues.issue: The gate metrics are uncalibrated against the channels they'll be measured on, which threatens the whole 'gates, not vibes' governance. A 15-minute median session and 65% retry rate are top-percentile numbers for browser arena games; portal traffic (the Phase 5 audience) medians a few minutes with huge drive-by bounce. Two failure modes: the project stalls in Phase 4 forever chasing an impossible gate, or the gates get quietly ignored and the discipline collapses. Worse, mixing itch-embed deep-players with portal drive-bys in one funnel makes the numbers uninterpretable.
issues.fix: Segment metrics by source from day one (itch embed vs direct link vs portal) and define gates on the engaged cohort (players who finish wave 1), not raw sessions. Recalibrate: ~50% engaged-retry and ~8-10 min engaged median are strong Phase 4 numbers for this genre. Add D1 return rate once CrazyGames is live — it's the metric their algorithm actually pays on.

issues.issue: GoatCounter cannot measure the gate metrics — it is privacy-focused pageview analytics with no custom event funnels, session stitching, or duration percentiles. 'Retry rate', 'runs per session', 'median session length', and 'wave-at-death histogram' all require an event pipeline. Listing it as a coequal option means risking Phase 1 shipping telemetry that can't answer Phase 2's exit criteria, forcing a re-instrumentation. Same gap: the Phase 0 'window.onerror reporter' has no destination until telemetry exists.
issues.fix: Drop GoatCounter from the plan; commit to PostHog free tier (or a 20-line POST to a Cloudflare Worker writing to KV, consistent with the Phase 6+ leaderboard plan) in Phase 1, with a fixed event schema written first: run_start, wave_reached, death(wave, cause), retry, block, dodge, settings_open. Route window.onerror into the same pipe. Verify events fire from inside the itch iframe (ad-blockers and iframe CSP eat third-party analytics — measure the loss rate).

issues.issue: Steam's AI-generated content disclosure (mandatory since January 2024) is never mentioned, yet the plan explicitly uses AI-assisted development, 'CC0 or generated' music, and 'AI-assisted UI localization'. This is a checkbox-level item that becomes a submission-blocker or a community-trust incident if discovered late — store pages have been review-bombed over undisclosed AI content. Separately, 'generated' music from a tool with unclear training-data licensing is a small but real takedown risk on a commercial release.
issues.fix: Add one line to Phase 5's Steam checklist: complete the AI disclosure honestly (AI-assisted code and localization; specify music provenance). For music, prefer verifiably CC0 (Kevin MacLeod-style attribution-free or commissioned for ~$50-200) over generative tools, or generate it procedurally with WebAudio like the SFX — on-brand with the zero-asset positioning and licensing-proof.

issues.issue: Mortal named allies ship one phase before the system that could replace them. Phase 3 removes free warband respawns for permadeath attachment, but ally recruitment/revival options only plausibly arrive with Phase 4's draft pool. The interim public beta therefore has pure downward snowball: lose an ally on wave 4, fight waves 5-15 understrength with no recourse — exactly the 'attrition fog' the vision statement promises to eliminate, shipped into the build that Show HN sees.
issues.fix: Move ally permadeath into Phase 4 and land it in the same release as draft options that touch the warband ('Recruit: a new named ally joins', 'Field medic: revive a fallen ally at half HP'). Loss is only compelling when the player had a choice about preventing or repairing it; until then keep respawns.

issues.issue: Early-phase durations assume near-full-time hours from a part-time dev. Phase 1 alone — a state-machine refactor of the scattered gameRunning/betweenWaves/player.alive flags across a 1430-line file, pause/auto-pause, a versioned persistence layer, death recap UI, keyboard attack, telemetry integration, AND recruiting and observing 5-10 strangers — is realistically 3-4 part-time weeks, not 'weeks 1-2' shared with Phase 0. The plan's later phases inherit this compounding optimism, and the burnout-risk section's 'fixed weekly hours' makes the math worse, not better.
issues.fix: State the actual hours/week budget at the top of the document and re-derive every phase from it (at 10-12 h/week, multiply current estimates by roughly 1.5-2x, landing 1.0 around 12-14 months — still fine). Alternatively keep the calendar and pre-cut: in Phase 1, telemetry and the death recap are the load-bearing items; the full state machine can degrade to 'pause + persistence bolted onto existing flags' with the refactor deferred to Tech Week.

issues.issue: No WebGL context-loss handling anywhere in the plan. Long sessions on integrated GPUs — precisely the Phase 3 target hardware and the portal audience — hit GPU resets and browser tab-discard context losses; r128 does not transparently recover, and the result is a frozen black canvas mid-run with no error. On CrazyGames this reads as 'game crashed, 1 star', and the planned window.onerror reporter won't even catch it (it's an event, not an exception).
issues.fix: Add to Phase 3's performance pass: listen for webglcontextlost/webglcontextrestored on the canvas; minimum viable is preventDefault plus a 'Graphics reset — click to reload' overlay that preserves the run's score to localStorage before reload. Log occurrences to telemetry to size the real-world rate.

issues.issue: Phase 0 contradicts itself: 'push to a private GitHub remote' and 'deploy to GitHub Pages' — Pages is unavailable on private repos under the free plan. Trivial, but it's the kind of snag that eats one of Phase 0's two days.
issues.fix: Pick one: itch.io alone is sufficient as the Phase 0 funnel (drop Pages), pay for GitHub Pro ($4/month), or keep the repo private and deploy the built artifact to Cloudflare Pages/Netlify free tier instead.

issues.issue: The marketing cadence is unbudgeted labor. 1-2 sub-15s GIFs per week across Bluesky/X/TikTok/Shorts for 36 weeks, plus devlogs, Discord moderation, replying to every demo comment, and weekly playtests — capture, edit, caption, post, engage is conservatively 2-3 hours/week, i.e. 15-25% of a part-time budget that the phase estimates already fully spend on development.
issues.fix: Budget it explicitly as a fixed weekly line item and cut cadence to match reality: one good GIF per week (the wolf-pack flank and guard-break clips genuinely carry themselves), batch-captured monthly, cross-posted with a scheduler; Discord stays low-touch (weekly playtest thread, not a community to run) until Phase 5. Marketing time comes out of the same hour budget as code — the roadmap currently pretends it's free.

verdict: Adopt-with-fixes. This is a far better roadmap than most solo devs ever write: safety-net-first ordering, validation before content, procedural-audio and zero-asset choices that dodge entire licensing categories, honest revenue expectations, gate metrics instead of vibes, and a 'We Will NOT Do' list that reads like someone who has actually shipped. The combat-first, wrap-don't-rebuild thesis is correct, and the codebase claims it rests on all verified against source. But four high-severity fixes are mandatory before adoption: (1) the Phase 6 content lock promises roughly 8-12 weeks of biomes/weapons/enemies/bosses that no phase schedules — shrink the lock or add the phase; (2) cut the three.js r128-to-r155 upgrade pre-1.0 — it is the plan's own 'rewrite for its own sake' wearing a lab coat, all risk to the hand-tuned feel with zero player payoff; (3) define what the $4.99 Steam buyer gets that three free web builds don't, before the store page exists, or launch reviews will write 'free in your browser' for you; (4) stop spending Show HN and r/WebGames — one-shot channels — on the Phase 3 beta that lacks the entire addiction loop the vision is named after. Below those: make localStorage survive the itch/CrazyGames iframes it will actually live in, spike the Tauri-vs-Electron Steam-overlay question months before it can sink Next Fest, anchor the calendar to a real fest date, and recalibrate the gate metrics per-channel so the governance mechanism doesn't get quietly abandoned. Apply the fixes and the realistic calendar is 12-14 months part-time rather than 9 — say that number out loud now, because the alternative is discovering it at week 30.
